rationale: The revision keeps the original high-precision policy while making boundary control more explicit. It targets recurring errors: spans that were too long, missing required words inside fixed expressions, inclusion of surrounding function words or complements, and overmarking of ordinary compositional phrases. It also broadens the description slightly so it remains useful for unseen projects without encoding development-set answers.
changes: Made the task wording slightly more language-neutral by referring to tokenized text rather than only English text.
Added guidance for conventional predicate/preposition patterns and established professional compounds while still requiring lexicalization.
Added explicit exclusions for ordinary accompaniment/time/modification prepositional phrases and auxiliary/modal/infinitive combinations.
Strengthened tight-boundary instructions: include required internal words, exclude complements and surrounding material, and avoid absorbing following noun phrases.
Added a conservative rule for fixed frames with variable slots: mark only fixed parts when discontinuous annotation is supported.
Kept the required structured-JSON response instruction and token-preservation instruction.
risks: Adding professional terms or established compounds may slightly increase false positives if annotators treat descriptive noun phrases as lexicalized.
The high-precision emphasis may continue to miss some valid but less obvious MWEs.
The fixed-frame/discontinuous guidance depends on whether the downstream annotation format supports discontinuous MWEs.
Language-neutral wording may be less specific for English-only edge cases, though the main English MWE categories are preserved.
